newsitem.title: GERMANY: Gaddum says euro not automatically stable as mark.
newsitem.headline: Gaddum says euro not automatically stable as mark.

text.p: Bundesbank vice-president Johann Wilhelm Gaddum said on Wednesday that it did not naturally follow that the future single European currency would be as stable as the deutschemark.
But he said a solid euro would contribute to peace and stability in the European region.
Gaddum also said that durable fulfilment of the criteria required to launch the euro was more important than meeting the numerical requirements with absolute precision.
Gaddum says euro not automatically stable as =2
Gaddum was specifically referring to the requirement calling on participants in the currency union to hold budget deficits at or below three percent of gross domestic product (GDP) in 1997.
Reining in deficits would remain a political goal, irrespective of the euro launch, he said.
Gaddum also said there was a case for setting exchange rates within the future EMU (Economic and Monetary Union) according to the parities operating in the European Monetary System.
A decision on EMU exchange rates should be taken as soon as possible, he added.
